issues.problem: Only the Tier 9 CA condenser is run, and only with one resonance value. No CA injector of any tier is ever run, so `injectorProgressMultiplier` and its exponents are never checked. Tiers 10 and 11 of the condenser are never run either. The 'change of resonance' in the Action is never done. The expected output count comes from `CaMachineRules.condenserOutput(1, 20.0D)`, the same production function, so the test checks itself rather than a value. The 'correct Tier' check reads the `CaSeries` arrays and the map size, not the registered blocks or the Tier data component on their items.
issues.reason: The AC needs all 3 condenser tiers and all 5 injector tiers to run representative recipes, and resonance changes compared against original values. A test that compares the implementation with itself cannot catch a wrong formula.
issues.fix: For every CA machine block, check its registered tier and its item's TIER component. Run each condenser tier with at least two resonance values (e.g. none and opa_resonator) and assert literal output counts (1 and 3). Run each injector tier with and without resonance and assert literal progress-per-tick and CE values.

history.note: fixed: 8機種の登録 Tier と Item の Tier を確認し、各機種を共鳴あり・なしで処理する GameTest に拡張しました。

issues.problem: Time, CE and progress are never measured on a running machine. The test only feeds `machine.overclockFactor()` into `TierManager.calculate`. Only the single four-overclocker combination is tried, so the G=1 case (F≤10, e.g. a single overclocker) is not compared. The FE converter check calls `EnergyConverterSpecification` directly, so the new link in `EnergyConverterBlockEntity` that reads adjacent overclockers is never exercised.
issues.reason: The AC asks to compare processing time, CE and progress on a processing machine with overclockers attached, and to confirm the CE converter keeps its own exponent in real use.
issues.fix: Start a real recipe on the grinder with overclockers attached. Assert its saved `required_progress`, `energy_per_progress` and `progress_per_tick`, and the CE consumed per tick, for at least one F≤10 and one F>10 combination. Place overclockers next to a real `EnergyConverterBlockEntity`, tick it, and assert the CE consumed and FE generated use the linear factor.

issues.problem: Each upgrade is placed alone, so the 64 cap is never checked independently. OPA alone gives exactly 1+63=64, and no combination that would go over 64 (e.g. OPA plus antimatter, or several upgrades on several faces) is tested.
issues.reason: The Expected Result requires the 64-item maximum to hold. As written, the test would pass even if the clamp were removed.
issues.fix: Put several upgrades on different faces whose total exceeds 64 (e.g. OPA + OEC), assert the limit is 64, and also assert an additive combination below the cap (e.g. antimatter + pure antimatter = 5).

The test now covers an additive case (5) and an over-cap case (64).

issues.problem: When a world reloads, the active recipe is re-checked by recomputing `TierManager.calculate(..., overclockFactor())` and `fixedOutputs(recipe)` from the current neighbours. If an overclocker or resonator was added or removed after the process started, `required_progress`, `energy_per_progress` or `pending_outputs` no longer match. The process is then aborted after the reload and its progress is lost.
issues.reason: The start-time values are already saved. Comparing them with values from neighbours that may have changed turns an allowed in-game action (placing an augment) into lost work after a save and reload.
issues.fix: Re-check only that the recipe still exists and matches the saved recipe data, not the augment-dependent multipliers. Alternatively, save the overclock factor and resonance used at start and compare against those.

history.note: fixed: 再読込時に現在の拡張配置から開始時の倍率・出力を再計算しないようにし、変更後の継続を GameTest で確認しました。
fixed: 再読込時に現在の拡張配置で開始時の値を再計算せず、配置変更後の処理継続を検証します。
Reload no longer recomputes the augment-dependent multipliers or outputs. A reload test was added.

issues.problem: `processingProgressMultiplier()` calls `AugmentScanner.resonance` on every tick of every CA injector. That reads 125 block states per tick per machine. The resonating collector does the same in `CaCollectorBlockEntity.tickServer`.
issues.reason: Resonance only changes when nearby blocks change. Rescanning a 5×5×5 volume every tick is a needless server cost, and the original caches the value instead of polling.
issues.fix: Compute resonance once when the process starts, store it with the other start-time parameters, and recompute only on neighbour or block changes (e.g. a dirty flag set from `neighborChanged`), not every tick.

issues.problem: All four `reactor/*_overclocker` recipes use `processingTicks(Integer.MAX_VALUE)` (2,147,483,647 ticks). This looks like a clamp, not the original reactor time, and none of the input counts or tiers are checked against the original.
issues.reason: A clamped value hides the original balance. Without laser acceleration the recipes can never finish in practice, so the overclockers cannot be obtained in survival.
issues.fix: Use the exact time from hotfix2 `CRecipes.recipeReactor` for each overclocker and record it in AGENTS.md. If the original value does not fit the `int` field, say so and choose a documented representation instead of silently clamping.

issues.problem: The code guards against infinite or overflowing resonance and multipliers (`Double.MAX_VALUE`, `Integer.MAX_VALUE`). The largest resonance the game can produce is 20^124 ≈ 1e161, which is finite, and outputs are clamped to the stack size anyway.
issues.reason: The code style says to check only states the game can actually produce.
issues.fix: Remove the infinity and overflow branches. Keep only the plain product and `(int)` conversion, with the existing `max(baseCount, …)`.

issues.problem: Excess fuel is always dropped at `y+1`, the block above the machine. That is where an energy storage upgrade or another solid block is often placed, so the dropped ItemEntity can spawn inside a solid block.
issues.reason: An item inside a solid block gets pushed out in an unpredictable direction or is hard to recover. This weakens the 'no item loss on removal' requirement.
issues.fix: Use `Containers.dropItemStack` at the machine's own position (as block-break drops do), or pick a free neighbouring face.

issues.problem: In the processing machine GUI, the energy clay fuel slot (64 energetic clay) sits on top of the player "Inventory" label. The stack count "64" is drawn over the letters "ry", and the bottom of the slot frame is cut off by the player-inventory background. Because of this, the screenshot cannot cleanly show the 64-item fuel count this criterion is meant to verify.
issues.reason: ClayMachineMenu places the fuel slot at (44,57), so the item is drawn at y 57–73 and the slot frame at y 56–74 (ClayMachineScreen.renderBg blits SLOT at leftPos+43, topPos+56). ClayMachineScreen also draws the "Inventory" label at inventoryLabelX=8, inventoryLabelY=72, and blits gui_playerinventory.png from topPos+72. The label (x≈8–58, y 72–80) and the inventory background therefore overlap the fuel slot (x 43–61, y 56–74).
issues.fix: Move the fuel slot and its label out of the player-inventory area. One option: keep imageHeight=166 and move the fuel slot up next to the "Tier N" text. Move the slot in ClayMachineMenu to e.g. (44,52) and the SLOT blit in ClayMachineScreen.renderBg to (43,51). Draw "Tier N" at y≈56 to the left of the slot (x 7–40). Then make sure nothing reaches past y=71. Another option: raise imageHeight and move the player inventory background, inventoryLabelY and the player slots down by the same amount, so the label starts at least 2 px below the slot frame (e.g. inventoryLabelY ≥ 76, inventory blit at ≥ topPos+76). After either change, the "64" count and the full slot frame should show with no text under them.
